entries.rationale: The Desktop sample owns the minimal managed window, local content, and lifecycle path.
Application composition, frontend assets, capabilities, and product UI are demonstrated by generated Runic Application templates and the Translations Editor.
The exact-package consumer publishes and runs Runic Desktop with trimming and NativeAOT enabled.
The Desktop sample covers the same minimal local-window outcome through the supported API.
A real Chromium bridge invokes typed managed capabilities and validates their results.
A real Chromium session exercises managed-to-JavaScript calls and correlated results.
Folder indexes, files, MIME types, HEAD, cache policy, and traversal rejection are tested.
Explicit file redirects and folder index fallback have independent behavioral coverage.
Virtual and streaming content handlers are tested with fallback, cancellation, disposal, and bridge priority.
Third-party model credentials and network application semantics belong to the consuming application, not presentation hosting.
Host-owned dependency injection and request-scoped content handling replace attaching a process-global custom server.
Typed embedded-window options and movement, sizing, visibility, and lifecycle capabilities cover frameless window behavior.
All-interface exposure fails closed unless the application supplies an explicit security policy.
The lock-backed generated React application is owned by Runic Application and Runic Vite rather than a Desktop-specific demo.
The native lifecycle fixture exercises window churn, bridge reconnect, cancellation, and shutdown; release acceptance requires a completed soak receipt.
Runic Translations Editor is the maintained production editor experience and exercises the supported Desktop topology.
Single-client denial and explicit multi-client admission with stable session identities are tested.
Generated Runic Application templates own the supported starter experience, frontend toolchain, diagnostics, and packaging path.
